sanskrit: tataḥ pravartitā samyak tapovidbhir dvijātibhiḥ śabde cārthe ca hetau ca eṣā prathamasargajā
english: Then this teaching was rightly set in motion by the twice-born who knew austerity, perfect in word, in meaning, and in reasoning—born of the first creation.

sanskrit: ādāv eva hi tac chāstram oṃkārasvarabhūṣitam ṛṣibhir bhāvitaṃ tatra yatra kāruṇiko hy asau
english: At the very beginning that scripture, adorned with the sound of Oṃ, was meditated upon by the seers in that place where the Compassionate One dwells.

sanskrit: tataḥ prasanno bhagavān anirdiṣṭaśarīragaḥ ṛṣīn uvāca tān sarvān adṛśyaḥ puruṣottamaḥ
english: Then the Blessed One, well pleased, his body undisclosed, unseen, the Supreme Person, spoke to all those seers.

sanskrit: kṛtaṃ śatasahasraṃ hi ślokānām idam uttamam lokatantrasya kṛtsnasya yasmād dharmaḥ pravartate
english: This supreme work of a hundred thousand verses has been composed, from which proceeds the dharma of the whole order of the world.

sanskrit: pravṛttau ca nivṛttau ca yonir etad bhaviṣyati ṛgyajuḥsāmabhir juṣṭam atharvāṅgirasais tathā
english: This shall be the source of both engagement and renunciation, honored by the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman, and by the Atharva-Āṅgirasa hymns as well.

sanskrit: tathā pramāṇaṃ hi mayā kṛto brahmā prasādajaḥ rudraś ca krodhajo viprā yūyaṃ prakṛtayas tathā
english: As it is authoritative, so too by me was Brahmā made, born of my grace, and Rudra, born of my wrath, O brahmins, and you yourselves as the primal natures.

sanskrit: sūryācandramasau vāyur bhūmir āpo 'gnir eva ca sarve ca nakṣatragaṇā yac ca bhūtābhiśabditam
english: The sun and moon, the wind, the earth, the waters, and fire too, and all the hosts of stars, and whatever is named as a created being—

sanskrit: adhikāreṣu vartante yathāsvaṃ brahmavādinaḥ sarve pramāṇaṃ hi yathā tathaitac chāstram uttamam
english: all abide within their offices, each according to its own; and as the expounders of Brahman are each authoritative, so is this supreme scripture.

sanskrit: bhaviṣyati pramāṇaṃ vai etan madanuśāsanam asmāt pravakṣyate dharmān manuḥ svāyaṃbhuvaḥ svayam
english: This my teaching shall be authoritative, and from it Manu, the self-existent one's son, shall himself proclaim the dharmas.

sanskrit: uśanā bṛhaspatiś caiva yadotpannau bhaviṣyataḥ tadā pravakṣyataḥ śāstraṃ yuṣmanmatibhir uddhṛtam
english: And when Uśanas and Bṛhaspati shall come into being, then they shall expound the scripture drawn forth from your own minds.

sanskrit: svāyaṃbhuveṣu dharmeṣu śāstre cośanasā kṛte bṛhaspatimate caiva lokeṣu pravicārite
english: When the dharmas of Svāyaṃbhuva, the scripture composed by Uśanas, and the doctrine of Bṛhaspati have been pondered throughout the worlds,

sanskrit: yuṣmatkṛtam idaṃ śāstraṃ prajāpālo vasus tataḥ bṛhaspatisakāśād vai prāpsyate dvijasattamāḥ
english: this scripture, made by you, shall the protector of his people, Vasu, then receive from Bṛhaspati, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: sa hi madbhāvito rājā madbhaktaś ca bhaviṣyati tena śāstreṇa lokeṣu kriyāḥ sarvāḥ kariṣyati
english: For that king shall be devoted in thought to me and shall be my worshipper, and by that scripture he shall perform all rites throughout the worlds.

sanskrit: etad dhi sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ śāstram uttamasaṃjñitam etad arthyaṃ ca dharmyaṃ ca yaśasyaṃ caitad uttamam
english: For this, of all scriptures, is the one named supreme; this is rich in meaning, conformable to dharma, and conducive to glory—this is the highest.

sanskrit: asya pravartanāc caiva prajāvanto bhaviṣyatha sa ca rājā śriyā yukto bhaviṣyati mahān vasuḥ
english: And by setting this in motion you shall be blessed with offspring, and that king, the great Vasu, shall be endowed with majesty.

sanskrit: saṃsthite tu nṛpe tasmiñ śāstram etat sanātanam antardhāsyati tat satyam etad vaḥ kathitaṃ mayā
english: But when that king has passed away, this eternal scripture shall vanish from sight. This is the truth I have declared to you.

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā vacanam adṛśyaḥ puruṣottamaḥ visṛjya tān ṛṣīn sarvān kām api prasthito diśam
english: Having spoken these words, the unseen Supreme Person dismissed all those seers and departed for some quarter unknown.

sanskrit: tatas te lokapitaraḥ sarvalokārthacintakāḥ prāvartayanta tac chāstraṃ dharmayoniṃ sanātanam
english: Then those fathers of the world, who meditate on the welfare of all worlds, set in motion that eternal scripture, the womb of dharma.

sanskrit: utpanne ''ṅgirase caiva yuge prathamakalpite sāṅgopaniṣadaṃ śāstraṃ sthāpayitvā bṛhaspatau
english: And when the son of Aṅgiras had come to be, in the first-ordained age, they established the scripture, with its limbs and Upaniṣads, in Bṛhaspati,

sanskrit: jagmur yathepsitaṃ deśaṃ tapase kṛtaniścayāḥ dhāraṇāt sarvalokānāṃ sarvadharmapravartakāḥ
english: and went, resolved upon austerity, to the region of their desire—they who sustain all the worlds and set in motion all the dharmas.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca tato 'tīte mahākalpe utpanne 'ṅgirasaḥ sute babhūvur nirvṛtā devā jāte devapurohite
english: Bhīṣma said: Then, when the great aeon had passed and the son of Aṅgiras had been born, the gods were content, for the chaplain of the gods had come into being.

sanskrit: bṛhad brahma mahac ceti śabdāḥ paryāyavācakāḥ ebhiḥ samanvito rājan guṇair vidvān bṛhaspatiḥ
english: "Vast," "Brahman," "great"—these are words that signify the same; endowed with these qualities, O king, was the learned Bṛhaspati.

sanskrit: tasya śiṣyo babhūvāgryo rājoparicaro vasuḥ adhītavāṃs tadā śāstraṃ samyak citraśikhaṇḍijam
english: His foremost pupil was the king Uparicara Vasu, who then studied thoroughly the scripture born of the Citraśikhaṇḍins.

sanskrit: sa rājā bhāvitaḥ pūrvaṃ daivena vidhinā vasuḥ pālayām āsa pṛthivīṃ divam ākhaṇḍalo yathā
english: That king Vasu, ordained beforehand by divine decree, ruled the earth as Indra, the Render-asunder, rules heaven.

sanskrit: tasya yajño mahān āsīd aśvamedho mahātmanaḥ bṛhaspatir upādhyāyas tatra hotā babhūva ha
english: That great-souled king held a great sacrifice, a horse-sacrifice, and Bṛhaspati, his preceptor, served there as the hotṛ priest.

sanskrit: prajāpatisutāś cātra sadasyās tv abhavaṃs trayaḥ ekataś ca dvitaś caiva tritaś caiva maharṣayaḥ
english: And there the three sons of Prajāpati were the assessors—Ekata, Dvita, and Trita, those great seers.

sanskrit: dhanuṣākṣo 'tha raibhyaś ca arvāvasuparāvasū ṛṣir medhātithiś caiva tāṇḍyaś caiva mahān ṛṣiḥ
english: Dhanuṣākṣa and Raibhya, Arvāvasu and Parāvasu, the seer Medhātithi too, and Tāṇḍya, the great seer,

sanskrit: ṛṣiḥ śaktir mahābhāgas tathā vedaśirāś ca yaḥ kapilaś ca ṛṣiśreṣṭhaḥ śālihotrapitāmahaḥ
english: the illustrious seer Śakti, and he who was Vedaśiras, and Kapila, best of seers, grandsire of Śālihotra,

sanskrit: ādyaḥ kaṭhas taittiriś ca vaiśaṃpāyanapūrvajaḥ kaṇvo 'tha devahotraś ca ete ṣoḍaśa kīrtitāḥ saṃbhṛtāḥ sarvasaṃbhārās tasmin rājan mahākratau
english: the first Kaṭha, and Taittiri, the forerunner of Vaiśaṃpāyana, Kaṇva, and Devahotra—these sixteen are renowned. All the appurtenances were gathered, O king, for that great rite.

sanskrit: na tatra paśughāto 'bhūt sa rājaivaṃ sthito 'bhavat ahiṃsraḥ śucir akṣudro nirāśīḥ karmasaṃstutaḥ āraṇyakapadodgītā bhāgās tatropakalpitāḥ
english: There was no slaying of any animal there; the king stood firm in this way—free of harm, pure, free of meanness, free of craving, lauded for his deeds—and the shares were apportioned there as chanted in the verses of the Āraṇyaka.

sanskrit: prītas tato 'sya bhagavān devadevaḥ purātanaḥ sākṣāt taṃ darśayām āsa so 'dṛśyo 'nyena kena cit
english: Then the Blessed One, the ancient God of gods, well pleased with him, showed himself to him in person, though he was unseen by any other.

sanskrit: svayaṃ bhāgam upāghrāya puroḍāśaṃ gṛhītavān adṛśyena hṛto bhāgo devena harimedhasā
english: He himself, smelling the share, took up the sacrificial cake; by the unseen God, whose intent is Hari, the share was carried off.

sanskrit: bṛhaspatis tataḥ kruddhaḥ sruvam udyamya vegitaḥ ākāśaṃ ghnan sruvaḥ pātai roṣād aśrūṇy avartayat
english: Then Bṛhaspati, enraged, swiftly raised the ladle, and striking at the sky with blows of the ladle, in his fury he let his tears flow.

sanskrit: uvāca coparicaraṃ mayā bhāgo 'yam udyataḥ grāhyaḥ svayaṃ hi devena matpratyakṣaṃ na saṃśayaḥ
english: And he said to Uparicara: "This share offered up by me was taken by the God himself, before my very eyes—of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: udyatā yajñabhāgā hi sākṣāt prāptāḥ surair iha kimartham iha na prāpto darśanaṃ sa harir vibhuḥ
english: For when sacrificial shares are offered up, the gods receive them here in person; why then has the all-pervading Hari not granted his appearance here?"

sanskrit: tataḥ sa taṃ samuddhūtaṃ bhūmipālo mahān vasuḥ prasādayām āsa muniṃ sadasyās te ca sarvaśaḥ
english: Then the great lord of earth, Vasu, and all the assessors together, soothed that agitated sage.

sanskrit: ūcuś cainam asaṃbhrāntā na roṣaṃ kartum arhasi naiṣa dharmaḥ kṛtayuge yas tvaṃ roṣam acīkṛthāḥ
english: And, unperturbed, they said to him: "You ought not to give way to anger; it is no part of dharma in the Kṛta age that you should have stirred up such wrath.

sanskrit: aroṣaṇo hy asau devo yasya bhāgo 'yam udyataḥ na sa śakyas tvayā draṣṭum asmābhir vā bṛhaspate yasya prasādaṃ kurute sa vai taṃ draṣṭum arhati
english: For that God, to whom this share was offered, is free of anger; he cannot be seen by you, nor by us, O Bṛhaspati. He upon whom He bestows His grace—he alone is worthy to behold Him."

sanskrit: ekatadvitatritā ūcuḥ vayaṃ hi brahmaṇaḥ putrā mānasāḥ parikīrtitāḥ gatā niḥśreyasārthaṃ hi kadā cid diśam uttarām
english: Ekata, Dvita, and Trita said: "We are renowned as the mind-born sons of Brahmā; once, for the sake of the highest good, we journeyed to the northern quarter.

sanskrit: taptvā varṣasahasrāṇi catvāri tapa uttamam ekapādasthitāḥ samyak kāṣṭhabhūtāḥ samāhitāḥ
english: For four thousand years we practiced the highest austerity, standing perfectly upon one foot, motionless as logs, our minds composed,

sanskrit: meror uttarabhāge tu kṣīrodasyānukūlataḥ sa deśo yatra nas taptaṃ tapaḥ paramadāruṇam kathaṃ paśyemahi vayaṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ tv iti
english: in the northern part of Meru, along the shore of the Ocean of Milk—that region where we performed our most terrible austerity, thinking, 'How might we behold the God Nārāyaṇa?'

sanskrit: tato vratasyāvabhṛthe vāg uvācāśarīriṇī sutaptaṃ vas tapo viprāḥ prasannenāntarātmanā
english: Then, at the final ablution of our vow, a bodiless voice spoke: 'Well practiced is your austerity, O brahmins, with an inmost self made serene.

sanskrit: yūyaṃ jijñāsavo bhaktāḥ kathaṃ drakṣyatha taṃ prabhum kṣīrodadher uttarataḥ śvetadvīpo mahāprabhaḥ
english: You are seekers, devoted—how shall you behold that Lord? North of the Ocean of Milk lies the White Island of great splendor.

sanskrit: tatra nārāyaṇaparā mānavāś candravarcasaḥ ekāntabhāvopagatās te bhaktāḥ puruṣottamam
english: There dwell men devoted to Nārāyaṇa, radiant as the moon, who have attained single-minded devotion, worshippers of the Supreme Person.

sanskrit: te sahasrārciṣaṃ devaṃ praviśanti sanātanam atīndriyā nirāhārā aniṣpandāḥ sugandhinaḥ
english: They enter into the eternal God of a thousand rays—beyond the senses, taking no food, motionless, sweetly fragrant.

sanskrit: ekāntinas te puruṣāḥ śvetadvīpanivāsinaḥ gacchadhvaṃ tatra munayas tatrātmā me prakāśitaḥ
english: Those single-hearted men dwell on the White Island; go there, O sages, for there my Self is made manifest.'

sanskrit: atha śrutvā vayaṃ sarve vācaṃ tām aśarīriṇīm yathākhyātena mārgeṇa taṃ deśaṃ pratipedire
english: Then, having all heard that bodiless voice, we made our way to that region by the path that had been told.

sanskrit: prāpya śvetaṃ mahādvīpaṃ taccittās taddidṛkṣavaḥ tato no dṛṣṭiviṣayas tadā pratihato 'bhavat
english: Reaching the great White Island, our hearts set upon Him, longing to behold Him—then the very range of our sight was struck back.

sanskrit: na ca paśyāma puruṣaṃ tattejohṛtadarśanāḥ tato naḥ prādurabhavad vijñānaṃ devayogajam
english: And we could not see the Person, our vision carried off by His radiance; then there arose in us a knowledge born of union with the God.

sanskrit: na kilātaptatapasā śakyate draṣṭum añjasā tataḥ punar varṣaśataṃ taptvā tātkālikaṃ mahat
english: Truly He cannot readily be beheld by one whose austerity is unperformed; so once more we practiced for a hundred years a great austerity suited to the hour.

sanskrit: vratāvasāne suśubhān narān dadṛśire vayam śvetāṃś candrapratīkāśān sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitān
english: At the close of our vow we beheld men most fair, white, resembling the moon, marked with every auspicious sign,

sanskrit: nityāñjalikṛtān brahma japataḥ prāgudaṅmukhān mānaso nāma sa japo japyate tair mahātmabhiḥ tenaikāgramanastvena prīto bhavati vai hariḥ
english: with hands ever folded, murmuring Brahman, facing the east and north. That muttered prayer, called the Mental, is murmured by those great-souled ones, and by that single-mindedness of theirs Hari is well pleased.

sanskrit: yā bhaven muniśārdūla bhāḥ sūryasya yugakṣaye ekaikasya prabhā tādṛk sābhavan mānavasya ha
english: What the radiance of the sun would be at the dissolution of an age, O tiger among sages, such was the splendor of each single one of those men.

sanskrit: tejonivāsaḥ sa dvīpa iti vai menire vayam na tatrābhyadhikaḥ kaś cit sarve te samatejasaḥ
english: 'That island is the abode of splendor,' so indeed we deemed; none there was greater than another, for all were equal in their radiance.

sanskrit: atha sūryasahasrasya prabhāṃ yugapad utthitām sahasā dṛṣṭavantaḥ sma punar eva bṛhaspate
english: Then suddenly we beheld, O Bṛhaspati, the splendor of a thousand suns risen all at once, once again.

sanskrit: sahitāś cābhyadhāvanta tatas te mānavā drutam kṛtāñjalipuṭā hṛṣṭā nama ity eva vādinaḥ
english: And those men ran swiftly forward together, their hands folded in cupped reverence, rejoicing, crying out only, 'Homage!'

sanskrit: tato 'bhivadatāṃ teṣām aśrauṣma vipulaṃ dhvanim baliḥ kilopahriyate tasya devasya tair naraiḥ
english: Then, as they uttered their praise, we heard a vast sound; an offering, it seemed, was being presented to that God by those men.

sanskrit: vayaṃ tu tejasā tasya sahasā hṛtacetasaḥ na kiṃ cid api paśyāmo hṛtadṛṣṭibalendriyāḥ
english: But we, our minds suddenly carried away by His radiance, could see nothing at all, our sight, strength, and senses borne away.

sanskrit: ekas tu śabdo 'virataḥ śruto 'smābhir udīritaḥ jitaṃ te puṇḍarīkākṣa namas te viśvabhāvana
english: But one sound, unceasing, we heard uttered: 'Victory to You, lotus-eyed One! Homage to You, maker of the universe!

sanskrit: namas te 'stu hṛṣīkeśa mahāpuruṣapūrvaja iti śabdaḥ śruto 'smābhiḥ śikṣākṣarasamīritaḥ
english: Homage be to You, Hṛṣīkeśa, firstborn of the great Person!'—such was the sound we heard, sounded forth in the syllables of correct articulation.

sanskrit: etasminn antare vāyuḥ sarvagandhavahaḥ śuciḥ divyāny uvāha puṣpāṇi karmaṇyāś cauṣadhīs tathā
english: In that interval a pure wind, bearing every fragrance, wafted divine flowers and herbs fit for the rite.

sanskrit: tair iṣṭaḥ pañcakālajñair harir ekāntibhir naraiḥ nūnaṃ tatrāgato devo yathā tair vāg udīritā vayaṃ tv enaṃ na paśyāmo mohitās tasya māyayā
english: By those single-hearted men, knowers of the five sacred times, Hari was worshipped; surely the God had come there, as their utterance declared—yet we did not see Him, bewildered by His māyā.

sanskrit: mārute saṃnivṛtte ca balau ca pratipādite cintāvyākulitātmāno jātāḥ smo 'ṅgirasāṃ vara
english: And when the wind had ceased and the offering had been made, we became troubled in mind with anxious thought, O best of the Āṅgirasas.

sanskrit: mānavānāṃ sahasreṣu teṣu vai śuddhayoniṣu asmān na kaś cin manasā cakṣuṣā vāpy apūjayat
english: Among those thousands of men of pure birth, not one honored us with so much as a thought or a glance.

sanskrit: te 'pi svasthā munigaṇā ekabhāvam anuvratāḥ nāsmāsu dadhire bhāvaṃ brahmabhāvam anuṣṭhitāḥ
english: Those hosts of sages too, self-possessed, vowed to the one Being, set no regard upon us, abiding in the state of Brahman.

sanskrit: tato 'smān supariśrāntāṃs tapasā cāpi karśitān uvāca khasthaṃ kim api bhūtaṃ tatrāśarīrakam
english: Then, as we were sorely wearied and wasted by our austerity, some being there, abiding in the sky, bodiless, addressed us:

sanskrit: dṛṣṭā vaḥ puruṣāḥ śvetāḥ sarvendriyavivarjitāḥ dṛṣṭo bhavati deveśa ebhir dṛṣṭair dvijottamāḥ
english: 'You have seen the white men, devoid of all sensory cravings; when these have been seen, the Lord of gods is seen, O best of the twice-born.

sanskrit: gacchadhvaṃ munayaḥ sarve yathāgatam ito 'cirāt na sa śakyo abhaktena draṣṭuṃ devaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: Go, all you sages, soon and the way you came; that God can in no way be seen by one without devotion.

sanskrit: kāmaṃ kālena mahatā ekāntitvaṃ samāgataiḥ śakyo draṣṭuṃ sa bhagavān prabhāmaṇḍaladurdṛśaḥ
english: In the fullness of a long time, by those who have attained single-heartedness, that Blessed One may indeed be seen—He who is hard to behold for His orb of radiance.

sanskrit: mahat kāryaṃ tu kartavyaṃ yuṣmābhir dvijasattamāḥ itaḥ kṛtayuge 'tīte viparyāsaṃ gate 'pi ca
english: But a great task is to be accomplished by you, O best of the twice-born, when this Kṛta age has passed and the reversal of things has come.

sanskrit: vaivasvate 'ntare viprāḥ prāpte tretāyuge tataḥ surāṇāṃ kāryasiddhyarthaṃ sahāyā vai bhaviṣyatha
english: In the age of Vaivasvata, O brahmins, when the Tretā age has come, you shall be helpers for accomplishing the task of the gods.'

sanskrit: tatas tad adbhutaṃ vākyaṃ niśamyaivaṃ sma somapa tasya prasādāt prāptāḥ smo deśam īpsitam añjasā
english: Then, having heard that wondrous speech, O drinker of soma, by His grace we readily reached the region of our desire.

sanskrit: evaṃ sutapasā caiva havyakavyais tathaiva ca devo 'smābhir na dṛṣṭaḥ sa kathaṃ tvaṃ draṣṭum arhasi nārāyaṇo mahad bhūtaṃ viśvasṛg ghavyakavyabhuk
english: Thus, even with our high austerity and with offerings to gods and ancestors, that God was not seen by us; how then could you be fit to see Him? Nārāyaṇa is the great Being, the maker of the universe, the eater of oblations to gods and ancestors."

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam ekatavākyena dvitatritamatena ca anunītaḥ sadasyaiś ca bṛhaspatir udāradhīḥ samānīya tato yajñaṃ daivataṃ samapūjayat
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus, conciliated by the speech of Ekata and by the counsel of Dvita and Trita, and by the assessors, the noble-minded Bṛhaspati then brought the sacrifice to completion and worshipped the deity.

sanskrit: samāptayajño rājāpi prajāḥ pālitavān vasuḥ brahmaśāpād divo bhraṣṭaḥ praviveśa mahīṃ tataḥ
english: His sacrifice ended, King Vasu too protected his people; but, fallen from heaven by a brahmin's curse, he thereafter entered the earth.

sanskrit: antarbhūmigataś caiva satataṃ dharmavatsalaḥ nārāyaṇaparo bhūtvā nārāyaṇapadaṃ jagau
english: And though gone within the earth, ever cherishing dharma, becoming wholly devoted to Nārāyaṇa, he chanted the word of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: tasyaiva ca prasādena punar evotthitas tu saḥ mahītalād gataḥ sthānaṃ brahmaṇaḥ samanantaram parāṃ gatim anuprāpta iti naiṣṭhikam añjasā
english: And by His grace alone he rose up once more, and passing from the surface of the earth he went straightway to the abode of Brahmā, attaining the supreme goal—such, truly, was his final consummation.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yadā bhakto bhagavata āsīd rājā mahāvasuḥ kimarthaṃ sa paribhraṣṭo viveśa vivaraṃ bhuvaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: When King Mahāvasu was a devotee of the Blessed One, why did he fall and enter a crevice of the earth?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam ṛṣīṇāṃ caiva saṃvādaṃ tridaśānāṃ ca bhārata
english: Bhīṣma said: On this too they tell this ancient tale, the dispute between the seers and the gods, O descendant of Bharata.

sanskrit: ajena yaṣṭavyam iti devāḥ prāhur dvijottamān sa ca chāgo hy ajo jñeyo nānyaḥ paśur iti sthitiḥ
english: "One must sacrifice with an aja," the gods told the best of the twice-born; "and by aja the goat is to be understood, no other beast"—such was their position.
